Database Connections and Transactions

Once you have made a decision on the database you will use and how you will interact with it, there are a couple of other features that can improve the performance and reliability of your application. Database connections define how your applications will connect to your database, and transactions define how multiple operations in a single unit of work will operate.

一旦你决定了要用哪个数据库以及如何与它交互，还有另外几个特性可以提升应用的性能和可靠性。数据库连接定义你的应用如何连接数据库，事务则定义单个工作单元中的多个操作将如何运作。

Database connections

When you first learned about databases and how to connect to them, you probably wrote code that allowed for a single connection. When you begin working with real-world applications, understanding proper connection management is crucial for performance and reliability. Most applications use a connection pool to reuse database connections instead of creating a new one for each operation.1

你最初学习数据库以及如何连接它们时，写的代码可能只允许一个连接。当你开始处理真实应用时，理解正确的连接管理对性能和可靠性至关重要。大多数应用使用连接池来复用数据库连接，而不是每次操作都新建一个。1

1 A connection pool is a cache of database connections maintained in memory so that they can be reused when future requests to the database are required, eliminating the overhead of repeatedly establishing new connections.
连接池是缓存在内存中的一组数据库连接，以便将来需要访问数据库时复用，省去反复建立新连接的开销。

The following example demonstrates how to use the Hikari Connection Pool (HikariCP) in Java to connect to a local PostgreSQL database:

下面的例子演示了如何在 Java 中使用 Hikari 连接池（HikariCP）连接本地 PostgreSQL 数据库：

// HikariCP connection pool configuration
HikariConfig config = new HikariConfig();
config.setJdbcUrl("jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/myapp");
config.setUsername("user");
config.setPassword("password");
config.setMaximumPoolSize(10);

HikariDataSource dataSource = new HikariDataSource(config);

If you’re using a framework like Spring in Java, this is automatically configured and handled underneath the hood for you.

如果你在 Java 中用 Spring 之类的框架，这些会被自动配置并在底层替你处理好。

Transactions

A database transaction is a logical unit of work containing one or more database operations (like insert, update, delete) executed as a single atomic operation that either completely succeeds or completely fails. The transaction maintains data integrity by ensuring that partial changes aren’t applied. The following example shows a money transfer between accounts, using a transaction to ensure that both operations succeed or both fail, maintaining the integrity of the account balance:

数据库事务是一个逻辑工作单元，包含一个或多个数据库操作（如 insert、update、delete），作为单个原子操作执行——要么完全成功，要么完全失败。事务通过确保部分更改不会被应用来维护数据完整性。下面的例子展示了账户间的转账，用一个事务确保两个操作要么都成功、要么都失败，从而维护账户余额的完整性：

// Concise transaction example
try (Connection conn = dataSource.getConnection()) {
    conn.setAutoCommit(false);
原书第 194 页
    try (PreparedStatement withdrawStmt =
            conn.prepareStatement(
                "UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ?");
     PreparedStatement depositStmt =
            conn.prepareStatement(
                "UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE id = ?")) {

        // Withdraw from source account
        withdrawStmt.setBigDecimal(1, amount);
        withdrawStmt.setLong(2, fromAccountId);
        withdrawStmt.executeUpdate();

        // Deposit to destination account
        depositStmt.setBigDecimal(1, amount);
        depositStmt.setLong(2, toAccountId);
        depositStmt.executeUpdate();

        conn.commit();
    } catch (SQLException e) {
        conn.rollback();
        throw e;
    }

Who Defines Transaction Boundaries?
谁来定义事务边界？

The responsibility of enforcing transactions depends on your database system and client setup. While databases typically guarantee ACID properties for properly defined transactions (as we’ll discuss in the next section), the application developer is usually responsible for defining transaction boundaries. You will need to ensure that related operations are grouped within the same transaction scope.
强制事务的责任取决于你的数据库系统和客户端设置。虽然数据库通常为正确定义的事务保证 ACID 特性（我们将在下一节讨论），但应用开发者通常负责定义事务边界。你需要确保相关操作被归到同一个事务范围内。

Consistency Models and Caching Strategies

You started out this chapter learning that data is the backbone of most applications you work on. This means that the foundation of any system lies in its ability to manage data reliably while delivering high performance. This section explores two critical concepts that address these needs: consistency models and caching strategies. While often discussed separately, these elements work together in modern data-driven applications to create a balance between data reliability and speed.

你在本章开头学到，数据是你所做大多数应用的骨架。这意味着任何系统的基础，在于它能否在交付高性能的同时可靠地管理数据。本节探讨满足这些需求的两个关键概念：一致性模型和缓存策略。虽然它们常常被分开讨论，但在现代数据驱动的应用中，这两者协同工作，在数据可靠性和速度之间取得平衡。

Consistency models

Building on the transaction concepts you learned earlier, consistency models define how your application will handle the accuracy of data across different parts of your system. While transactions maintain data integrity on individual operations, consistency models determine how that integrity is maintained across multiple servers or when multiple users access the same information simultaneously.

在你前面学到的事务概念基础上，一致性模型定义你的应用将如何处理系统不同部分之间的数据准确性。事务在单个操作上维护数据完整性，而一致性模型决定这种完整性如何跨多台服务器维护，或在多用户同时访问同一信息时如何维护。

原书第 195 页

Consistency in databases refers to the guarantee that any transaction will bring the database from one valid state to another, ensuring that all data adheres to defined rules, constraints, and relationships without contradiction. This principle is one of the four ACID properties (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability) that ensure reliable transaction processing in database systems.

数据库中的一致性，指的是任何事务都会把数据库从一个有效状态带到另一个有效状态的保证，确保所有数据都遵循定义好的规则、约束和关系，不产生矛盾。这条原则是四个 ACID 特性（原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性）之一，它们保证数据库系统中事务处理的可靠性。

Types of consistency models. Applications have different needs for how quickly changes to data should appear everywhere in the system. Databases offer various consistency models to meet these requirements:

一致性模型的类型。对于数据的更改应该多快在系统各处显现，不同应用有不同的需求。数据库提供各种一致性模型来满足这些要求：

  • Strong consistency: Guarantees that each part of your system sees the same data at the same time, with changes appearing in the exact order they occurred. In PostgreSQL, when you update a user’s account balance, all subsequent reads immediately reflect that change. As a result of this, the system may temporarily block operations to maintain this guarantee, prioritizing accuracy over availability.强一致性：保证系统的每个部分在同一时间看到相同的数据，更改按发生的确切顺序显现。在 PostgreSQL 中，当你更新一个用户的账户余额后，所有后续读取立刻反映该更改。这样做的结果是，系统可能会临时阻塞操作来维持这个保证，把准确性置于可用性之上。
  • Eventual consistency: Prioritizes keeping your application running by allowing temporary inconsistencies that resolve over time. In Amazon DynamoDB, updating a product price might take seconds to propagate globally. The result is that users in different regions could briefly see different prices, but the system remains available during outages. This mode works well when immediate consistency isn’t critical.最终一致性：允许临时的不一致随时间解决，以此优先保证应用持续运行。在 Amazon DynamoDB 中，更新一个商品价格可能需要几秒钟才能全局传播。结果是不同地区的用户可能短暂地看到不同价格，但系统在故障期间保持可用。当即时一致性不是关键时，这种模式很适用。
  • Causal consistency: Maintains order only between causally related operations. In collaborative editing tools like Google Docs, if User A comments on User B’s edit, everyone sees the edit before the comment, but unrelated edits from User C might appear in different orders to different users. This provides a middle ground between strong and eventual consistency.因果一致性：只在有因果关系的操作之间维持顺序。在 Google Docs 这类协同编辑工具中，如果用户 A 对用户 B 的编辑发表评论，每个人都会先看到编辑、再看到评论，但用户 C 的不相关编辑可能在不同用户那里以不同顺序出现。它在强一致性和最终一致性之间提供了一个中间地带。
  • Session consistency: Ensures consistency within individual user sessions while allowing differences between users. In ecommerce applications, once you add an item to your cart, you’ll always see it there during your session, even if other users’ views of inventory might be slightly outdated. This creates a consistent experience for each user without requiring global synchronization.会话一致性：在单个用户会话内保证一致性，同时允许不同用户之间存在差异。在电商应用中，一旦你把一件商品加入购物车，在你的会话期间你总会看到它在那儿，即使其他用户看到的库存可能稍有滞后。这为每个用户创造了一致的体验，而不需要全局同步。

CAP theorem and its implications. The CAP theorem explains a fundamental trade-off in distributed systems. When your data is spread across multiple servers, you can guarantee only two of these three properties simultaneously:

CAP 定理及其含义。CAP 定理解释了分布式系统中的一个根本权衡。当你的数据分布在多台服务器上时，你只能同时保证以下三个特性中的两个：

  • Consistency: All servers show the same data at the same time.一致性：所有服务器在同一时间显示相同的数据。
    • 原书第 196 页
  • Availability: The system continues working even if some servers fail.可用性：即使某些服务器故障，系统继续工作。
  • Partition tolerance: The system continues working even if network connections between servers break.分区容忍性：即使服务器之间的网络连接断开，系统继续工作。

These trade-offs create the following system designs:

这些权衡产生了以下系统设计：

  • CP systems: CP systems prioritize consistency and partition tolerance at the expense of availability. If there’s a network problem, the system might stop accepting requests rather than risk showing incorrect data. Examples include traditional banking applications, inventory management systems, and financial services where data accuracy is critical. Technologies like Apache HBase and Google Spanner fall into this category.CP 系统：CP 系统以牺牲可用性为代价，优先保证一致性和分区容忍性。如果出现网络问题，系统可能停止接受请求，而不是冒险显示错误数据。例子包括传统银行应用、库存管理系统以及数据准确性至关重要的金融服务。Apache HBase 和 Google Spanner 等技术属于这一类。
  • AP systems: AP systems focus on availability and partition tolerance, accepting eventual consistency. These systems are ideal for content delivery networks, social media feeds, and recommendation engines where immediate consistency is less critical than system uptime. Technologies like Amazon DynamoDB and Cassandra are good examples of this approach. It’s better to show a slightly outdated social media post than to make the entire feed unavailable.AP 系统：AP 系统专注于可用性和分区容忍性，接受最终一致性。这些系统非常适合内容分发网络、社交媒体信息流和推荐引擎，在这些场景里即时一致性不如系统在线时间重要。Amazon DynamoDB 和 Cassandra 等技术是这种做法的好例子。显示一条稍微过时的社交媒体帖子，也比让整个信息流不可用要好。
  • CA systems: CA systems offer consistency and availability but cannot tolerate network partitions. These systems work well in single-node databases or tightly coupled clusters on reliable networks. Traditional Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS) like MySQL or PostgreSQL configured without distributed capabilities operate in this mode.CA 系统：CA 系统提供一致性和可用性，但无法容忍网络分区。这些系统在单节点数据库或可靠网络上紧耦合的集群中表现良好。没有配置分布式能力的传统关系数据库管理系统（RDBMS），如 MySQL 或 PostgreSQL，就运行在这种模式下。

Choosing the right consistency model. Modern applications will often employ multiple consistency models for different data types within the same system. The key here is to match the consistency requirements to the business impact.

选择合适的一致性模型。现代应用通常会在同一系统中对不同数据类型采用多种一致性模型。这里的关键是让一致性需求与业务影响相匹配。

Use strong consistency for operations where accuracy is critical and temporary unavailability is acceptable. Financial transactions, inventory updates, and user authentication typically require this approach.

对于准确性至关重要、且临时不可用可接受的操作，使用强一致性。金融交易、库存更新和用户认证通常需要这种方式。

原书第 197 页

Use eventual consistency for data where slight delays are acceptable and availability is crucial. User activity logs, recommendation systems, and content feeds can tolerate temporary inconsistencies in exchange for better performance and uptime.

对于轻微延迟可接受、可用性至关重要的数据，使用最终一致性。用户活动日志、推荐系统和内容信息流可以容忍临时的不一致，以换取更好的性能和在线时间。

Use session consistency for user-facing features where individual consistency matters more than global synchronization. Shopping carts, user preferences, and draft content work well with this model.

对于面向用户的功能，当单个用户的一致性比全局同步更重要时，使用会话一致性。购物车、用户偏好和草稿内容很适合这种模型。

When choosing the right consistency model, remember that this is not permanent. The important part of this process is understanding the requirements as they exist right now, balancing the trade-offs, and selecting the appropriate model.

选择合适的一致性模型时，记住这不是一劳永逸的。这个过程中重要的是理解当下的需求、权衡利弊、并选择合适的模型。

Optimizing performance with caching

Caching is a technique that stores frequently used data in faster storage locations to reduce response time and database load. It’s like keeping your most-used apps on your phone’s home screen instead of searching through all your apps each time. When your application requests data, the cache serves as a quick-access storage layer between your application and the database.

缓存是一种把频繁使用的数据存储在更快的存储位置、以减少响应时间和数据库负载的技术。这就像把你最常用的 app 放在手机主屏幕上，而不是每次都翻遍所有 app。当你的应用请求数据时，缓存充当应用和数据库之间的快速访问存储层。

When you make a database call, even a simple one, network calls and disk reads are involved that can take tens or hundreds of milliseconds. A cache stores data in memory, reducing response times by 10× to 100× or more, depending on the context and architecture.

当你发起一次数据库调用时，哪怕是很简单的调用，也涉及网络请求和磁盘读取，可能耗时几十到几百毫秒。缓存在内存中存储数据，根据上下文和架构不同，可将响应时间缩短 10 到 100 倍甚至更多。

However, caching comes with trade-offs. It introduces complexity regarding data freshness and adds another potential point of failure. This is why defining a caching strategy is critical. A good strategy determines how your application manages the relationship between cached data and the source of truth in your database.

然而，缓存也有代价。它在数据新鲜度方面引入了复杂性，并增加了另一个潜在的故障点。这就是为什么定义缓存策略至关重要。一个好的策略决定了你的应用如何管理缓存数据与数据库中真相源之间的关系。

Common caching strategies. Modern applications use three primary caching strategies, each with different trade-offs among performance, consistency, and complexity:

常见的缓存策略。现代应用主要使用三种缓存策略，每一种在性能、一致性和复杂性之间有不同的权衡：

Cache-aside (lazy loading). With cache-aside, your application code is responsible for managing both the cache and the database. When a request is made for data, your application will first check the cache to see whether it’s available. If the data is unavailable (a cache miss), the application retrieves the data from the database and stores it in the cache for future requests. If the data is available (a cache hit), the application retrieves it from the cache.

旁路缓存（懒加载）。使用旁路缓存时，你的应用代码负责同时管理缓存和数据库。当请求数据时，应用先查缓存看数据是否在里面。如果数据不在（缓存未命中），应用从数据库取回数据并存入缓存供以后请求使用。如果数据在（缓存命中），应用直接从缓存取。

In the following example, a blog post is looked up in the cache by its ID. If the ID is found, the application will return that post. If not, the application will find the blog post in the database and then store it in the cache for the next request:

在下面的例子中，一篇博客文章按 ID 在缓存中查找。如果 ID 找到了，应用就返回那篇文章。如果没找到，应用从数据库中查出文章，然后存入缓存供下次请求使用：

原书第 198 页
public BlogPost getPostById(Long id) {
    BlogPost cached = cache.get(id);
    if (cached != null) return cached;

    BlogPost post = database.findById(id);
    cache.put(id, post);

    return post;
}

This strategy works well for read-heavy applications where you want fine-grained control over what gets cached. The trade-off is that your application code becomes more complex, and the first request for any piece of data will always be slower because of the cache lookup and miss.

这种策略很适合读多的应用，尤其是当你想对缓存什么做细粒度控制时。代价是你的应用代码变得更复杂，而且对任何数据的第一次请求总是更慢，因为有缓存查找和未命中。

Write-through. With write-through caching, every write operation updates both the cache and database simultaneously. This ensures that both the database and cache contain the same data but can slow performance since the write happens in both locations. In the following example, the database and cache are updated within the same method:

写穿（write-through）。使用写穿缓存时，每次写操作同时更新缓存和数据库。这确保数据库和缓存包含相同的数据，但因为写要发生在两个地方，可能拖慢性能。在下面的例子中，数据库和缓存在同一个方法里更新：

public void updatePost(BlogPost post) {
    database.save(post);
    cache.put(post.getId(), post);
}

This strategy works well when you need strong consistency between your cache and database, and when read performance is more important than write performance. The trade-off is slower performance on writes and potentially caching data that might not get read often.

当你需要缓存和数据库之间的强一致性、且读性能比写性能更重要时，这种策略很适用。代价是写性能变慢，而且可能缓存了不常被读的数据。

Write-behind (write-back). Write-behind caching writes the data to the cache immediately but will update the database asynchronously. This gives you fast performance on your write operations but introduces the risk of data loss if the cache fails before the database is updated. In the following example, the cache is updated, and then a background process is spawned to update the database:

异步回写（write-behind / write-back）。异步回写缓存把数据立即写入缓存，但异步更新数据库。这让写操作性能很快，但如果缓存数据库更新之前就故障，就有数据丢失的风险。在下面的例子中，缓存先更新，然后启动一个后台进程来更新数据库：

public void updatePost(BlogPost post) {
    cache.put(post.getId(), post);
    asyncQueue.schedule(() -> database.save(post));
}

This strategy works well for write-heavy applications that can handle some risk of data loss in exchange for better performance. Some examples of the write-behind strategy include user activity, logging, or metrics where losing some data points is acceptable.

这种策略很适合写多的应用——这类应用可以容忍一定的数据丢失风险以换取更好的性能。异步回写策略的一些例子包括用户活动、日志或指标，在这些场景里丢失一些数据点是可以接受的。

When to use caching. Caching is a powerful tool in your toolbelt, but it doesn’t come without trade-offs. A cache is another moving part in your system that can fail, go stale, or consume resources. The question isn’t whether caching is good or bad, but whether the benefits of adding it to your application justify the added complexity.

什么时候用缓存。缓存是你工具带上的一件利器，但它并非没有代价。缓存是你系统中又一个会出故障、变陈旧或消耗资源的运转部件。问题不在于缓存是好是坏，而在于把它加入你的应用所带来的好处，是否值回那份增加的复杂性。

原书第 199 页

Consider an online store’s product catalog. When a user visits the store and searches for a product, the application needs to retrieve information from multiple tables like product details, inventory, reviews, and pricing. If each product page takes an average of 200 ms to complete and 1,000 shoppers are using the store simultaneously, your application could be making 4,000 requests to the database in a short period of time. The database must handle this high volume of simultaneous queries while maintaining acceptable response times.

想想一家在线商店的产品目录。当用户访问商店并搜索一个商品时，应用需要从多个表中检索信息，比如商品详情、库存、评价和定价。如果每个商品页面平均需要 200 毫秒完成，同时有 1000 个购物者在使用商店，你的应用在短时间内可能向数据库发起 4000 次请求。数据库必须处理这么高的并发查询量，同时维持可接受的响应时间。

Most of these requests are for information that rarely changes. Here, caching makes sense because you can serve requests at an average of 5 ms from memory while your database handles the truly dynamic operations like order processing.

这些请求大多是针对很少变化的信息。在这里，缓存是合理的，因为你可以平均用 5 毫秒从内存响应请求，而让数据库去处理订单处理这类真正动态的操作。

Let’s compare this to another scenario like a real-time trading platform where prices change multiple times per second. Even if you were to set a cache eviction policy (removing data from the cache) at 30-second intervals, you could still be displaying outdated prices, potentially costing your users money. The complexity of cache invalidation and the risk of displaying stale data here far outweigh the performance benefits.

我们把它和另一个场景对比，比如一个实时交易平台，价格每秒变动多次。即使你设置每 30 秒驱逐一次缓存（把数据从缓存中移除），你仍可能显示过时价格，让用户赔钱。在这里，缓存失效的复杂性和显示陈旧数据的风险，远远超过性能收益。

When evaluating whether caching is right for a particular scenario, ask yourself these questions:

评估缓存是否适合某个特定场景时，问问自己这些问题：

  • How often does this data change?这些数据多久变一次？
  • What are the costs of serving users stale data?给用户提供陈旧数据的代价是什么？
  • How expensive are my current queries?我当前的查询有多昂贵？
  • Are there any current performance bottlenecks?当前有没有性能瓶颈？

The answers to these questions will guide you toward the right solution for your specific use case.

这些问题的答案会指引你为具体用例找到正确的方案。

Caching and consistency. Caching introduces its own challenges when it comes to consistency, which you learned about earlier in this section. When you cache data, you’re creating a temporary copy that might become stale when the original data changes. Different caching strategies handle this differently:

缓存与一致性。在一致性方面，缓存引入了它自己的挑战——你在本节前面已经学过。当你缓存数据时，你创建了一个临时副本，当原始数据变化时它可能变陈旧。不同的缓存策略对此处理方式不同：

  • Cache-aside with TTL (time to live) provides eventual consistency by automatically expiring cached data after a set time.带 TTL（存活时间）的旁路缓存通过在设定时间后自动过期缓存数据，提供最终一致性。
  • Write-through caching maintains strong consistency between cache and database but at the cost of write performance.写穿缓存维持缓存与数据库之间的强一致性，但代价是写性能。
  • Write-behind caching accepts temporary inconsistency in favor of performance.异步回写缓存为了性能接受临时的不一致。
原书第 200 页

The key is weighing the trade-offs with your business requirements. In the financial world, data might require write-through caching for strong consistency, while a personal blog could use cache-aside with eventual consistency through TTL expiration.

关键是根据业务需求权衡。在金融领域，数据可能需要写穿缓存来获得强一致性，而个人博客可以使用旁路缓存，通过 TTL 过期获得最终一致性。

Distributed Systems Considerations
分布式系统注意事项

When your application scales across multiple servers, you face additional challenges:
当你的应用扩展到多台服务器时，你会面临额外的挑战：
  • Cache consistency becomes more complex.缓存一致性变得更复杂。
  • Distributed transactions may be necessary.可能需要分布式事务。
  • You might need to implement eventual consistency patterns.你可能需要实现最终一致性模式。
  • Data replication and sharding strategies become important.数据复制和分片策略变得重要。
These topics deserve their own chapter, but be aware that as your application grows, your persistence strategy will need to evolve.
这些话题值得单独用一章来讲，但你要知道，随着应用的成长，你的持久化策略也需要演进。

Planning for Data Growth

As you have learned throughout this chapter, there is no “perfect” plan when it comes to your data, but you should avoid going in with no plan at all. Putting some thought into your data strategy up front can save you significant effort, time, and stress later. Planning for growth means regularly reviewing performance metrics and capacity needs. This is best done as a joint effort among the development team, database administrators, and operations staff. Watch for key indicators like query response times exceeding acceptable thresholds, database CPU consistently above a certain percentage, memory usage climbing steadily, or an increase in user complaints about slow load times. These conversations should happen monthly for growing applications, allowing you to address issues before they become critical.

正如你在本章学到的，在数据方面没有“完美”的计划，但你应该避免毫无计划就上马。预先花点心思制定数据战略，可以为你以后省下大量精力、时间和压力。为增长做规划意味着定期审视性能指标和容量需求。这件事最好由开发团队、数据库管理员和运维人员共同完成。留意这些关键指标：查询响应时间超过可接受阈值、数据库 CPU 持续高于某个百分比、内存使用稳步攀升、或用户抱怨加载慢的次数增加。对于成长中的应用，这些讨论应该每月进行一次，让你在问题变得紧急之前就处理掉它们。

Using scaling strategies

When growth indicators appear, you have several options, each appropriate for different situations:

当增长指标出现时，你有几个选项，每个适用于不同的情况：

  • Vertical scaling: Adds more resources (CPU, RAM) to your database server. This is often your first move because it’s simple and doesn’t require architectural changes, but you’ll eventually hit hardware limits.垂直扩展：给数据库服务器增加更多资源（CPU、内存）。这通常是你的第一步，因为它简单、不需要架构改动，但你最终会碰到硬件上限。
    • 原书第 201 页
  • Horizontal scaling: Distributes your data across multiple servers. This becomes necessary when vertical scaling reaches its limits or when you need geographic distribution for global applications.水平扩展：把数据分布到多台服务器上。当垂直扩展达到上限、或你需要为全球应用做地理分布时，这就变得必要。
  • Read replicas: Create copies of your database for read operations, reducing load on the primary database. Consider this approach first for read-heavy applications. This is easier to implement than full horizontal scaling and can provide significant performance improvements.只读副本：为读操作创建数据库副本，减轻主数据库的负载。对于读多的应用，优先考虑这种方式。它比完整的水平扩展更容易实现，并且能带来显著的性能提升。
  • Sharding: Partitions your data across multiple databases based on a shard key. This is the most complex option but necessary for applications with massive data volumes that can’t fit on a single server.分片：根据分片键把数据分区到多个数据库上。这是最复杂的选项，但对于单台服务器装不下的海量数据应用来说是必要的。

Read Replicas Versus Caching
只读副本与缓存

While read replicas and caching improve read performance, they work differently:
虽然只读副本和缓存都提升读性能，但它们的工作方式不同：
  • Read replicas are complete copies of your database that stay synchronized with the primary database through replication.只读副本是你数据库的完整副本，通过复制与主数据库保持同步。
  • Caching stores frequently accessed data in memory as a temporary copy that may become stale.缓存在内存中存储频繁访问的数据作为临时副本，它可能变陈旧。
Read replicas provide eventual consistency at the database level and don’t require application code changes, while caching requires your application to manage cache invalidation and consistency. Read replicas are particularly useful for geographic distribution and read-heavy workloads, whereas caching excels at reducing response times for frequently accessed data.
只读副本在数据库层面提供最终一致性，不需要改应用代码；而缓存需要你的应用管理缓存失效和一致性。只读副本对地理分布和读多的工作负载特别有用，而缓存擅长降低频繁访问数据的响应时间。

Maintaining performance during growth

Regular data maintenance becomes increasingly important as your application scales. You can maintain performance as follows:

随着应用扩展，定期的数据维护变得越来越重要。你可以通过以下方式维持性能：

  • Implement data archiving strategies for old data to keep working sets manageable.对旧数据实施归档策略，让工作集保持可管理。
  • Set up appropriate database indexes and review them regularly as query patterns evolve.建立适当的数据库索引，并随查询模式演进定期审查。
  • Schedule regular database maintenance tasks like analyzing query performance and optimizing slow queries.安排定期的数据库维护任务，如分析查询性能和优化慢查询。
原书第 202 页

Understanding various database types and levels of persistence abstractions can help you make informed decisions about the architecture and direction of your application. The right choice depends on your application’s requirements and the skills of your team, and there is no universal best solution.

理解各种数据库类型和持久化抽象层次，能帮你对应用的架构和方向做出明智决策。正确的选择取决于应用的需求和团队的技能，没有放之四海而皆准的最佳方案。

Querying and Managing Data Performance

A slow application will frustrate users, no matter how good it looks. While the backend team focuses on getting data to users, it sometimes forgets about performance; the team is happy as long as the application works. Whether you’re building a small web application or a complex enterprise system, the way you query and manage data can make or break your applications’ performance.

一个慢的应用会让用户沮丧，无论它看起来多漂亮。后端团队专注于把数据送到用户手里时，有时会忘记性能；只要应用能跑，团队就高兴。无论你做的是小型 Web 应用还是复杂的企业系统，你查询和管理数据的方式，可能决定应用性能的成败。

This section covers the fundamentals of efficient data access knowledge that can help you avoid performance issues in the future. These core principles are so common that you’ll encounter them across many applications. You’ll learn practical techniques for optimizing queries, understand database indexing, and discover when to use specific performance tools. These skills will not only enhance your applications’ performance but also demonstrate your deep understanding of database fundamentals.

本节讲述高效数据访问的基础知识，帮你在未来避开性能问题。这些核心原则非常普遍，你会在许多应用中遇到它们。你将学习优化查询的实用技巧、理解数据库索引、并发现何时使用特定的性能工具。这些技能不仅会提升应用的性能，还能展示你对数据库基础的深刻理解。

Efficient Query Writing

When you’re getting started, you just want to write the query that gets the results you’re looking for. The next step should be to ask, “How can I improve the performance of this query?” Understanding how to write efficient queries is a fundamental skill that dramatically impacts your application’s performance. A poorly optimized query can consume excessive server resources, create bottlenecks, and lead to a frustrating user experience.

刚起步时，你只想写出能拿到想要结果的查询。下一步应该是问：“我怎么提升这个查询的性能？”理解如何写高效查询是一项基本功，它会显著影响应用的性能。优化糟糕的查询会消耗过多服务器资源、造成瓶颈、并导致令人沮丧的用户体验。

The difference between a good and poorly optimized query can be huge, sometimes reducing execution time from seconds to milliseconds. Let’s explore some essential techniques that will help you optimize your data access and build applications that remain responsive even under high throughput.

一个优化良好的查询和一个优化糟糕的查询之间的差别可能巨大，有时能把执行时间从几秒降到几毫秒。我们来探讨一些必不可少的技巧，帮你优化数据访问，构建即使在高吞吐量下也能保持响应的应用。

Basic query optimization

The first step in writing efficient queries is understanding what makes them inefficient in the first place. Consider this common scenario:

写高效查询的第一步，是先理解是什么让查询变得低效。看看这个常见场景：

public List<User> getAllActiveUsers() {
    return jdbcTemplate.query(
        "SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = true",
        (rs, rowNum) -> {
            User user = new User();
            user.setId(rs.getLong("id"));
            user.setUsername(rs.getString("username"));
原书第 203 页
            user.setEmail(rs.getString("email"));
            user.setActive(rs.getBoolean("active"));
            user.setCreatedAt(rs.getTimestamp("created_at"));
            // ... mapping 15 more fields
            return user;
        });
}

This query looks innocent enough, but it has two significant issues. First, SELECT * retrieves all columns from the database, even if you need only one or two. Second, it’s loading potentially thousands of records into memory at once. Let’s improve it:

这个查询看起来人畜无害，但它有两个大问题。第一，SELECT * 从数据库取出所有列，即使你只需要一两列。第二，它可能一次性把成千上万条记录载入内存。我们来改进它：

public List<UserSummary> getActiveUserSummaries() {
    return jdbcTemplate.query(
        "SELECT id, username, email FROM users WHERE active = true LIMIT 100",
        (rs, rowNum) -> {
            UserSummary summary = new UserSummary();
            summary.setId(rs.getLong("id"));
            summary.setUsername(rs.getString("username"));
            summary.setEmail(rs.getString("email"));
            return summary;
        });
}

By selecting only the columns you need and limiting the result set, you’ve dramatically reduced the amount of data transferred from the database to your application. This simple change can improve performance by orders of magnitude, especially when dealing with large tables.

通过只选择需要的列并限制结果集，你大幅减少了从数据库传输到应用的数据量。这个简单的改动可以把性能提升几个数量级，尤其是在处理大表时。

Be Specific About Columns
明确指定列

Always be specific about the columns you select and consider using pagination (splitting results into smaller chunks like 20 records per page) when retrieving large sets of data. Not only does this improve performance, but it also makes your code more maintainable by clearly documenting exactly what data your application needs.
始终明确指定你要选择的列，并在检索大数据集时考虑使用分页（把结果拆成较小块，比如每页 20 条记录）。这不仅提升性能，还通过清晰记录应用到底需要什么数据，让代码更易维护。

Prepared statements

Once you have gone through some basic query optimizations, the next step is to make sure the database can execute it as efficiently as possible. A prepared statement is a precompiled SQL query that lets you safely insert data values at runtime while improving performance and preventing SQL injection. In the following example, the statement is constructed by concatenating values directly into SQL:

做完一些基本查询优化后，下一步是确保数据库能尽可能高效地执行它。预处理语句是预编译的 SQL 查询，让你在运行时安全地插入数据值，同时提升性能并防止 SQL 注入。在下面的例子中，语句是通过把值直接拼进 SQL 构造的：

public User findUserByEmailAndStatus(String email, boolean active) {
    String sql = "SELECT id, username, email FROM users WHERE email = '" +
                 email + "' AND active = " + active;
    return jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(sql, User.class);
}
原书第 204 页

Every time this method executes, the database must parse, compile, and optimize a completely new query. Now compare it with a prepared statement:

每次这个方法执行时，数据库都必须解析、编译和优化一个全新的查询。现在把它和预处理语句对比：

public User findUserByEmailAndStatus(String email, boolean active) {
    return jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(
        "SELECT id, username, email FROM users WHERE email = ? AND active = ?",
        new Object[]{email, active},
        User.class);
}

With prepared statements, the database parses and optimizes the query once, then reuses that execution plan for subsequent calls with different parameters. This query plan caching can reduce execution time by 20%–50% for frequently executed queries. Beyond performance, prepared statements automatically handle parameter escaping, protecting your application from SQL injection attacks without requiring manual input sanitization.

使用预处理语句时，数据库只解析和优化查询一次，然后对后续不同参数的调用复用那个执行计划。对于频繁执行的查询，这种查询计划缓存可以把执行时间减少 20% 到 50%。除了性能，预处理语句还自动处理参数转义，无需手动清理输入就能保护应用免受 SQL 注入攻击。

Index management

Imagine trying to find relevant mentions of “caching” in this entire book without an index. You would have to read every single page, taking notes along the way. Database indexes solve the same problem by creating a looking table that maps values directly to where they are stored, transforming slow full-table scans into fast retrievals. In the following example, the query has no indexes and will take approximately 2,000 ms to execute:

想象一下，如果没有索引，你要在整本书里找“缓存”这个词的相关提及。你得一页一页读，一路做笔记。数据库索引解决同样的问题——它创建一个查找表，把值直接映射到存储位置，把缓慢的全表扫描变成快速检索。在下面的例子中，查询没有索引，大约需要 2000 毫秒执行：

// Query execution time without an index: ~2000ms
UserProfile profile = jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(
    "SELECT * FROM user_profiles WHERE email = ?",
    new Object[]{"john.doe@example.com"},
    UserProfile.class);

Without an index on the email column, the database performs a full table scan. Now, let’s add an index:

email 列上没有索引，数据库执行全表扫描。现在我们加一个索引：

CREATE INDEX idx_user_profiles_email ON user_profiles(email);

With this index, the same query might now execute in 5 ms instead of 2,000 ms, a 400× improvement! However, indexes aren’t free. They take up storage space and slow down write operations because the database must update each index when data changes.

有了这个索引，同一个查询现在可能 5 毫秒就执行完，而不是 2000 毫秒——提升了 400 倍！然而，索引不是免费的。它们占用存储空间，并且拖慢写操作，因为数据变化时数据库必须更新每个索引。

When deciding what to index, consider these guidelines:

决定对什么建索引时，请考虑以下准则：

  • Index columns used frequently in WHERE clauses.对 WHERE 子句中频繁使用的列建索引。
  • Index columns used in JOIN conditions.对 JOIN 条件中使用的列建索引。
  • Index columns used in ORDER BY or GROUP BY clauses.对 ORDER BY 或 GROUP BY 子句中使用的列建索引。
原书第 205 页
  • Consider composite indexes for queries that filter on multiple columns.对多列过滤的查询考虑组合索引。
  • Avoid indexing columns with low cardinality (few unique values).避免对低基数（唯一值很少）的列建索引。

Handling large result sets

When you’re working in development, one of the easiest problems to overlook is the sheer volume of data that might exist in your production environment. Without a large dataset, it’s easy to forget that returning large collections of objects in production can cause performance issues. As mentioned earlier, one way to address this is by limiting the number of records returned in a query. This is where pagination comes into play, by allowing you to navigate through the results in manageable chunks.

在开发环境工作时，最容易忽视的问题之一，就是生产环境中可能存在的数据量。没有大数据集，你很容易忘记在生产环境返回大对象集合会导致性能问题。前面提到过，解决方法之一是限制查询返回的记录数。分页在这里派上用场，它让你以可管理的块浏览结果。

In the following example, a Java method retrieves paginated product data filtered by category. The method executes two database queries: one to fetch the specific page of products and another to get the total count. The method then assembles these results into a page object containing both the product data and pagination metadata needed for the client application:

在下面的例子中，一个 Java 方法检索按分类过滤的分页产品数据。该方法执行两条数据库查询：一条取指定页的产品，另一条取总数。然后方法把这些结果组装成一个页面对象，既包含产品数据，也包含客户端应用所需的分页元数据：

public Page<Product> getProductsByCategory(String category, int page, int size) {
    int offset = page * size;

    List<Product> products = jdbcTemplate.query(
        "SELECT id, name, price FROM products WHERE category = ? " +
        "ORDER BY name LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
        new Object[]{category, size, offset},
        (rs, rowNum) -> {
            Product product = new Product();
            product.setId(rs.getLong("id"));
            product.setName(rs.getString("name"));
            product.setPrice(rs.getBigDecimal("price"));
            return product;
        });

    int totalCount = jdbcTemplate.queryForObject(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE category = ?",
        new Object[]{category},
        Integer.class);

    return new Page<>(products, page, size, totalCount);
}

This approach has a potential performance issue: the second query counting all matching rows can become expensive as the table grows. The code uses offset-based pagination, which requires the database to scan and discard all rows before the offset point, becoming increasingly inefficient with larger offsets.

这种方式有一个潜在的性能问题：随着表变大，第二条统计所有匹配行的查询会变得昂贵。代码使用基于偏移量的分页，这要求数据库扫描并丢弃偏移点之前的所有行，偏移越大效率越低。

原书第 206 页

Here are some alternatives to consider:

这里有一些替代方案可以考虑：

  • Replace offset pagination with keyset pagination (using WHERE id > last_seen_id).用键集分页替代偏移量分页（使用 WHERE id > last_seen_id）。
  • Cache count results when they don’t change frequently.当计数不频繁变化时，缓存计数结果。
  • Estimate counts for very large datasets.对超大数据集估算计数。
  • Consider UI patterns like infinite scroll that don’t require total counts.考虑无限滚动这类不需要总数的 UI 模式。

Tools and Best Practices

Consider the old adage, “If a tree falls in a forest and no one is around to hear it, does it make a sound?” Now imagine your users are in that forest hearing the tree fall on your database while you’re at home, completely unaware of what’s happening. Problems will inevitably arise, but the key question is: how will you gain visibility into those issues?

想想那句老话：“如果一棵树在森林里倒下而没有人听见，它发出声音了吗？”现在想象你的用户就在那片森林里，听到树砸在你的数据库上，而你却在家里，完全不知道发生了什么。问题不可避免会出现，但关键问题是：你要如何获得对这些问题的可见性？

Understanding query execution plans

A database query planner (also called an optimizer) is a critical component of any database management system that translates your SQL statements into executable programs called execution plans. Think of it as a compiler that takes your SQL code and determines the most efficient way to retrieve the requested data.

数据库查询规划器（也叫优化器）是任何数据库管理系统的关键组件，它把你的 SQL 语句翻译成称为执行计划的可执行程序。把它想象成一个编译器，接收你的 SQL 代码，决定检索所请求数据的最高效方式。

What is a database query planner? Query planners work by analyzing your SQL query, considering available indexes, table statistics, and various execution strategies to generate an optimal plan. Query planners have two main types: rule-based optimizers follow strict rules (like always using available indexes), and cost-based optimizers generate multiple execution plans and select the one with the lowest estimated cost. Most modern database systems use cost-based optimizers.

什么是数据库查询规划器？查询规划器通过分析你的 SQL 查询、考虑可用索引、表统计信息和各种执行策略来生成最优计划。查询规划器主要有两种类型：基于规则的优化器遵循严格规则（比如总是使用可用索引）；基于代价的优化器生成多个执行计划，并选择估计代价最低的那个。大多数现代数据库系统使用基于代价的优化器。

Database-specific query planners. Each database system has its own query planner with unique features:

各数据库专属的查询规划器。每个数据库系统都有自己的查询规划器，各有独特特性：

  • PostgreSQL: PostgreSQL’s planner/optimizer creates an execution plan by generating possible plans for scanning each relation (table) in the query, determining which indexes to use, and examining different join sequences to find the cheapest one. For complex queries with many joins, PostgreSQL uses a genetic query optimizer to find a reasonable (though not necessarily optimal) plan in a reasonable time.PostgreSQL：PostgreSQL 的规划器/优化器通过为查询中的每个关系（表）生成可能的扫描计划、决定使用哪些索引、并考察不同的连接顺序以找到代价最低的那个，来创建执行计划。对于连接很多的复杂查询，PostgreSQL 使用遗传查询优化器，在合理时间内找到一个合理（但不一定最优）的计划。
  • MySQL: MySQL’s query optimizer also uses a cost-based approach, focusing on optimizing read operations where it particularly excels. It evaluates different access methods, join types, and join orders to find the most efficient execution plan.MySQL：MySQL 的查询优化器也使用基于代价的方法，专注于优化它尤其擅长的读操作。它评估不同的访问方法、连接类型和连接顺序，以找到最高效的执行计划。
原书第 207 页
  • Oracle: Oracle’s optimizer is highly sophisticated and offers additional enterprise-level features for optimization, including adaptive execution plans that can change during query execution based on runtime statistics.Oracle：Oracle 的优化器非常精密，提供额外的企业级优化特性，包括能在查询执行期间根据运行时统计信息改变的自适应执行计划。

Using query execution plans. Most databases provide the EXPLAIN command to view the execution plan for a query. Here’s how to use it:

使用查询执行计划。大多数数据库提供 EXPLAIN 命令来查看查询的执行计划。下面是用法：

-- Basic EXPLAIN in PostgreSQL
EXPLAIN SELECT u.username, p.bio
FROM users u JOIN profiles p ON u.id = p.user_id
WHERE u.active = true;

-- More detailed analysis with EXPLAIN ANALYZE (PostgreSQL)
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT u.username, p.bio
FROM users u JOIN profiles p ON u.id = p.user_id
WHERE u.active = true;

-- MySQL EXPLAIN format
EXPLAIN SELECT u.username, p.bio
FROM users u JOIN profiles p ON u.id = p.user_id
WHERE u.active = true;

EXPLAIN is supported by PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, and other major database systems, though the syntax and output format may vary. PostgreSQL and MySQL also offer EXPLAIN ANALYZE, which runs the query and provides additional information about how the optimizer’s expectations matched the execution.

EXPLAIN 被 PostgreSQL、MySQL、Oracle 和其他主流数据库系统支持，尽管语法和输出格式可能不同。PostgreSQL 和 MySQL 还提供 EXPLAIN ANALYZE，它会实际运行查询，并提供关于优化器预期与实际执行匹配程度的额外信息。

The execution plan output typically shows the following:

执行计划输出通常显示以下内容：

  • Which tables will be accessed and in what order将访问哪些表以及以什么顺序
  • What join methods will be used (nested loop, merge join, hash join)将使用什么连接方法（嵌套循环、归并连接、哈希连接）
  • Which indexes (if any) will be used for each table每个表将使用哪些索引（如果有）
  • What types of scans will be performed (sequential scan, index scan)将执行什么类型的扫描（顺序扫描、索引扫描）
  • Estimated and/or actual costs in terms of time and resources在时间和资源方面的估计和/或实际代价
  • Row counts (estimated versus actual when using ANALYZE)行数（使用 ANALYZE 时为估计值与实际值对比）
原书第 208 页

Learning to read execution plans takes practice but is one of the most valuable skills for debugging slow queries. When analyzing plans, look for warning signs like these:

学会阅读执行计划需要练习，但它是调试慢查询最有价值的技能之一。分析计划时，寻找以下这些警示信号：

  • Full table scans when indexes should be used本该用索引却在做全表扫描
  • Inefficient join methods for the data volume对于数据量来说低效的连接方法
  • Missing or unused indexes缺失或未使用的索引
  • High estimated costs or row counts过高的估计代价或行数
  • Large discrepancies between estimated and actual values (when using ANALYZE)估计值与实际值之间差异很大（使用 ANALYZE 时）

Regular use of EXPLAIN helps you understand how your database thinks and makes decisions, allowing you to write more efficient queries and design better schemas and indexes.

定期使用 EXPLAIN 帮你理解数据库是怎么思考和做决策的，让你能写出更高效的查询、设计更好的 schema 和索引。

Compare Plans Across Environments
跨环境对比执行计划

Beyond optimizing individual queries, comparing execution plans across environments (development, staging, production) can reveal critical deployment issues. Environment inconsistencies like missing indexes, outdated statistics, or different data distributions can cause queries that perform well in testing to fail in production. When performance suddenly degrades after a deployment, comparing execution plans across environments often reveals the root cause faster than other debugging approaches.
除了优化单个查询，跨环境（开发、预发、生产）对比执行计划还能揭示关键的部署问题。环境不一致——比如缺索引、统计信息过时、或数据分布不同——会导致在测试中表现良好的查询在生产环境出问题。当部署后性能突然下降时，跨环境对比执行计划往往比其他调试方法更快找到根因。

Database monitoring and analysis

Understanding how your queries perform under ideal conditions by using EXPLAIN is important, but real-world performance depends on how your application interacts with the database under load. Simply relying on database-native tools like slow query logs or statistics tables (pg_stat_statements) gives only part of the picture.

用 EXPLAIN 理解查询在理想条件下的表现很重要，但真实性能取决于负载下应用如何与数据库交互。仅仅依赖慢查询日志或统计表（pg_stat_statements）这类数据库原生工具，只能看到部分图景。

To get a holistic view, you need to incorporate monitoring from the application’s perspective. This is where application-level observability comes in, providing insights into how database interactions affect overall application health and performance.

要获得全局视图，你需要从应用的视角加入监控。这就是应用层可观测性的用武之地，它提供关于数据库交互如何影响整体应用健康和性能的洞见。

In software engineering, observability refers to how well you can understand the internal state of a system based on the outputs it produces.

在软件工程中，可观测性指的是你能在多大程度上根据系统产生的输出来理解其内部状态。

Modern application frameworks often provide powerful tools for observability, integrating metrics, logging, and tracing. Spring Boot, through its Actuator module and the Micrometer metrics library, excels at this, offering deep insights into database interactions with minimal configuration.

现代应用框架通常提供强大的可观测性工具，集成指标、日志和追踪。Spring Boot 通过 Actuator 模块和 Micrometer 指标库在这方面表现出色，只需最少配置就能提供对数据库交互的深入洞见。

Here are the key concepts to learn when talking about observability:

谈论可观测性时，以下是需要学习的关键概念：

  • Logging: Recording events and errors, which can be correlated with metrics and traces to diagnose issues.日志：记录事件和错误，可与指标和追踪关联来诊断问题。
  • Metrics: Gathering quantitative data about system performance. For databases, this includes connection pool usage (active, idle, pending connections), query execution times, transaction times, and error rates.指标：收集关于系统性能的定量数据。对于数据库，这包括连接池使用情况（活跃、空闲、等待的连接）、查询执行时间、事务时间和错误率。
原书第 209 页
  • Tracing: Following a request as it propagates through different parts of your application and even across distributed systems. This helps pinpoint where latency occurs, including time spent in database calls.追踪：跟踪一个请求在应用不同部分甚至跨分布式系统中的传播。这有助于精确定位延迟发生在哪里，包括数据库调用花费的时间。

Here are some real-world scenarios where observability provides actionable insights:

以下是一些可观测性能提供可执行洞见的真实场景：

  • Is the connection pool a bottleneck? High values for jdbc.connections.pending metrics indicate threads are waiting too long for a connection. Seeing jdbc.connections.active constantly hitting the jdbc.connections.max limit suggests the pool is too small or connections aren’t being released properly (potential leaks or long-running transactions).连接池是瓶颈吗？jdbc.connections.pending 指标偏高说明线程等连接等太久。如果看到 jdbc.connections.active 一直顶到 jdbc.connections.max 上限，说明池太小，或者连接没有被正确释放（可能泄漏或有长事务）。
  • Are we wasting database resources? If jdbc.connections.active is consistently low, while jdbc.connections.idle is high, your pool might be oversized, consuming unnecessary memory and database resources.我们在浪费数据库资源吗？如果 jdbc.connections.active 持续偏低而 jdbc.connections.idle 偏高，你的池可能过大，消耗了不必要的内存和数据库资源。
  • Why is a specific user request slow? Distributed tracing can show you the entire lifecycle of a request. If a trace reveals that 90% of the request time is spent in a single database span (representing a query or transaction), you know exactly where to focus your optimization efforts (likely needing EXPLAIN on that specific query).某个特定用户请求为什么慢？分布式追踪能展示请求的整个生命周期。如果追踪显示 90% 的请求时间花在单个数据库 span（代表一次查询或事务）上，你就确切知道该把优化精力集中在哪里（很可能需要对那个查询跑 EXPLAIN）。
  • Is there an N + 1 query problem? A trace might show dozens of rapid, small database queries being executed sequentially within one logical operation. This classic N + 1 problem, often originating from ORM mapping misconfigurations, becomes immediately visible in a trace.存在 N + 1 查询问题吗？追踪可能显示在一个逻辑操作内顺序执行了几十个快速的小数据库查询。这个经典的 N + 1 问题（常源于 ORM 映射配置错误）在追踪中立刻可见。
  • Are specific queries getting slower over time? By monitoring metrics for query execution time (if enabled) and correlating them with application deployments or data growth, you can proactively identify queries that need optimization before they cause major incidents.某些查询是不是随时间变慢了？通过监控查询执行时间指标（如果开启了的话），并把它们与应用部署或数据增长关联起来，你可以在查询引发重大事故之前主动发现需要优化的查询。
  • How do database errors impact users? Correlating database error logs or metrics spikes with application-level error rates or failed request traces helps understand the user impact of database issues (e.g., constraint violations, deadlocks, connectivity problems).数据库错误如何影响用户？把数据库错误日志或指标尖峰与应用层错误率或失败请求追踪关联起来，有助于理解数据库问题对用户的影响（比如约束违反、死锁、连接问题）。

Spring Boot Actuator exposes production-ready endpoints for monitoring, while Micrometer provides a vendor-neutral application metrics facade. When used together, they can automatically instrument your DataSource beans (like HikariCP, the default in Spring Boot) to collect many of the vital statistics we’ve mentioned, providing the raw data needed to gain these insights.

Spring Boot Actuator 暴露用于监控的生产就绪端点，而 Micrometer 提供厂商中立的应用指标门面。两者一起使用时，它们可以自动对你的 DataSource bean（如 Spring Boot 默认的 HikariCP）插桩，收集我们提到的许多关键统计数据，提供获得这些洞见所需的原始数据。

Balancing complexity and performance

As a software engineer, one of the most critical skills you’ll develop is making informed decisions about trade-offs in your code. This is particularly evident when working with databases, where you often need to balance code readability and maintainability against query performance. Let’s explore this balancing act with a real-world scenario involving order processing.

作为软件工程师，你要培养的最关键技能之一，就是对代码中的权衡做出明智决策。这在处理数据库时尤为明显——你常常需要在代码可读性、可维护性与查询性能之间取得平衡。我们用一个涉及订单处理的真实场景来探索这种平衡。

In the following example, we’ll look at two approaches to fetching order data. The first approach uses Spring Data JPA with method chaining and stream operations; it’s clean and easy to understand, but may not perform well at scale. The second approach uses raw SQL; it’s more efficient but requires more careful maintenance:

在下面的例子中，我们看两种获取订单数据的方式。第一种使用 Spring Data JPA 的方法链和流操作；它干净易懂，但在大规模下可能性能不佳。第二种使用原始 SQL；它更高效，但需要更仔细的维护：

// Simple but potentially inefficient approach
List<Order> recentOrders =
orderRepository.findByUserIdAndStatusOrderByCreatedAtDesc(
    userId, OrderStatus.COMPLETED);

List<OrderDto> result = recentOrders.stream()
    .filter(order -> order.getTotal().compareTo(new BigDecimal("100.00")) > 0)
    .map(orderMapper::toDto)
    .collect(Collectors.toList());

// More efficient but complex approach
List<OrderDto> efficientResult = jdbcTemplate.query(
    """
    SELECT o.id, o.created_at, o.total, u.name AS user_name
    FROM orders o JOIN users u ON o.user_id = u.id
    WHERE o.user_id = ? AND o.status = ? AND o.total > 100.00
    ORDER BY o.created_at DESC
    """,
    new Object[]{userId, OrderStatus.COMPLETED.name()},
    (rs, rowNum) -> {
        OrderDto dto = new OrderDto();
        dto.setId(rs.getLong("id"));
        dto.setCreatedAt(rs.getTimestamp("created_at"));
        dto.setTotal(rs.getBigDecimal("total"));
        dto.setUserName(rs.getString("user_name"));
        return dto;
    });

The second approach is more efficient because it pushes filtering to the database and retrieves only necessary data. However, it’s also more complex and tightly coupled to the database structure.

第二种方式更高效，因为它把过滤下推到数据库，只检索必要的数据。然而，它也更复杂，并且与数据库结构紧耦合。

When deciding between approaches, consider these factors:

在两种方式间做决定时，请考虑以下因素：

  • The scale of your data你的数据规模
  • Performance requirements性能要求
  • Maintenance overhead维护开销
    • 原书第 211 页
  • Team familiarity with SQL团队对 SQL 的熟悉程度
  • Future flexibility needs未来的灵活性需求

Often, a hybrid approach works best: use ORM for most operations and drop to raw SQL for performance-critical paths.

通常，混合方式效果最好：大多数操作用 ORM，性能关键的路径才降到原始 SQL。

Efficient data access isn’t just about fast queries; it’s about understanding the entire data lifecycle in your application. By selecting only the data you need, leveraging appropriate indexes, using pagination for large result sets, and monitoring performance, you can build applications that remain responsive even as your data grows.

高效的数据访问不只是查询快；它关乎理解应用中数据的整个生命周期。通过只选择需要的数据、利用适当的索引、对大型结果集使用分页、以及监控性能，你可以构建即使数据增长也能保持响应的应用。

Data Migration and Transformation

Data migration is a common challenge that every software engineer faces at some point. Development teams regularly need to upgrade database systems between database types (such as migrating from relational to NoSQL databases or vice versa), connect with external services, or combine data from multiple sources. These tasks happen frequently throughout your career. Understanding how to properly handle data migration and transformation is a core skill.

数据迁移是每位软件工程师都会在某个时刻面临的常见挑战。开发团队经常需要在不同数据库类型之间升级数据库系统（比如从关系数据库迁移到 NoSQL，或反之）、连接外部服务、或合并来自多个来源的数据。这些任务在你的职业生涯中频繁出现。理解如何正确处理数据迁移和转换是一项核心技能。

In this section, you’ll learn the essentials of data migration and transformation, including strategies for moving data between systems, handling schema changes, and ensuring data integrity throughout the process. These skills will help you tackle these challenges with confidence and avoid common mistakes that could lead to data loss or corruption.

在本节中，你将学习数据迁移和转换的基本知识，包括在系统间移动数据的策略、处理 schema 变更、以及在整个过程中确保数据完整性。这些技能将帮你自信地应对这些挑战，避免可能导致数据丢失或损坏的常见错误。

Understanding Data Movement Fundamentals

As a software engineer, one of your primary tools in your tool belt is your ability to solve problems. On the surface, the problem of moving data from one system to another might seem pretty straightforward. All you need to do is just copy the data from one system and paste it in another, right? Unfortunately, the process is rarely that simple. A successful data migration requires careful planning, execution, and validation.

作为软件工程师，你工具带上最主要的工具之一就是解决问题的能力。表面上看，把数据从一个系统移到另一个系统的问题似乎很直接。你只需要把数据从一个系统复制粘贴到另一个，对吧？不幸的是，过程很少那么简单。一次成功的数据迁移需要仔细的规划、执行和验证。

The good news is that you can use some really helpful migration strategies as templates for moving your data from one system to another. Like every decision you make, the strategy you choose depends on factors such as data volume, system complexity, available downtime windows, risk tolerance, and business requirements. Understanding these factors will help you select the most appropriate approach for your specific migration scenario.

好消息是，你可以用一些非常有用的迁移策略作为模板，把数据从一个系统移到另一个。和你做的每个决定一样，你选的策略取决于数据量、系统复杂度、可用的停机窗口、风险承受力和业务需求等因素。理解这些因素将帮你为具体的迁移场景选择最合适的方式。

原书第 212 页

Big bang versus phased migration

Big bang migration moves all the data at one time, usually during a downtime window. This can be an easier approach but also comes with a lot of risk. Let’s use the example of moving employees from one database to another. In a big bang approach, you might move all the employees in the entire database over to a new one.

大爆炸式迁移一次性移动所有数据，通常在停机窗口内进行。这可能是更简单的方式，但也伴随大量风险。我们用把员工数据从一个数据库移到另一个的例子。在大爆炸方式中，你可能把整个数据库里的所有员工一次性移到新库。

In contrast, a phased migration moves data in stages. You are still probably doing this in a downtime timeframe, but you’re moving only a segment of the data, validating and then moving onto another segment of data. In our employee example, maybe you move only employees from HR in this phase. This is where careful planning comes into play as it will help determine how you will divide this phased migration. You can start with the group or groups that might feel the impact the least if something does go wrong.

相比之下，分阶段迁移分阶段移动数据。你可能还是在停机时间内做，但每次只移动一部分数据、验证、然后再移动下一部分。在员工的例子里，也许这个阶段你只移 HR 部门的员工。这时候仔细的规划就派上用场了，它会帮你决定如何划分这次分阶段迁移。你可以从那些即使出问题受影响也最小的部门开始。

If you have never worked on a data migration project, starting with a phased approach might be the safer strategy. While it might take longer, it significantly reduces the risk and gives you the opportunity to learn early on before moving on to more critical data.

如果你从未做过数据迁移项目，从分阶段方式开始可能是更安全的策略。虽然它可能更慢，但它显著降低风险，并让你在处理更关键数据之前就有机会及早学习。

Process Data in Batches
分批处理数据

If you’re processing these datasets in code, make sure to process them in batches to avoid overwhelming system memory. A batch of 1,000 to 10,000 records may typically be a good starting point, but this is where you want to perform proof-of-concept (PoC) tests to determine your system’s capabilities.
如果你在代码中处理这些数据集，务必分批处理，以免压垮系统内存。一批 1000 到 10000 条记录通常是个不错的起点，但这正是你要做概念验证（PoC）测试来确定系统能力的地方。

ETL processes

ETL (extract, transform, load) is a process for moving data between systems:

ETL（抽取、转换、加载）是在系统间移动数据的过程：

  • Extract: Pulls data from the source system抽取：从源系统拉取数据
  • Transform: Converts data to match the target system’s format and requirements转换：把数据转换成符合目标系统格式和要求的样子
  • Load: Inserts the transformed data into the target system加载：把转换后的数据插入目标系统

This three-step approach clearly defines the boundaries of each process. While isolated as part of a larger process, each one of these steps will present its own challenges. During extraction, you might encounter rate limits or performance impacts on production systems. Transformation often presents data quality issues that weren’t visible during smaller PoC testing. Loading can trigger constraints or validation failures in the target system.

这种三步法清晰定义了每个过程的边界。虽然作为更大过程的一部分被隔离开，但每一步都会带来自己的挑战。抽取时，你可能遇到限流或对生产系统的性能影响。转换常常暴露出在较小 PoC 测试中不可见的数据质量问题。加载可能触发目标系统中的约束或校验失败。

原书第 213 页

While implementing an ETL process, you will need to invest time in detailed error handling and logging to catch and identify issues. You will want to know when and why records failed to migrate so that you can quickly iterate on the process.

实现 ETL 过程时，你需要投入时间做详细的错误处理和日志记录，以捕获和识别问题。你会想知道记录何时、为何迁移失败，以便快速迭代这个过程。

Data synchronization

In some cases, you will need to keep multiple systems in sync during a transition period. Let’s go back to our employee database example where you took a phased migration approach. While this mitigates risk, it does present another challenge: as you onboard new employees, they will need to exist in both databases until the phased migration is complete.

在某些情况下，你需要在过渡期内保持多个系统同步。回到员工数据库的例子，你采取了分阶段迁移方式。虽然这降低了风险，但它确实带来了另一个挑战：随着你录入新员工，他们需要同时存在于两个数据库中，直到分阶段迁移完成。

For synchronization scenarios consider using the following:

对于同步场景，考虑使用以下方式：

  • Message queues to handle updates asynchronously消息队列来异步处理更新
  • Change data capture (CDC) to track database modifications变更数据捕获（CDC）来跟踪数据库修改
  • Reconciliation processes to identify and fix inconsistencies对账流程来识别和修复不一致

In this section, you learned some data migration and transformation strategies for moving data between systems. In the next section, you’ll learn how to make changes to the underlying database schema.

在本节中，你学习了一些在系统间移动数据的数据迁移和转换策略。在下一节中，你将学习如何对底层数据库 schema 做变更。

Handling Schema Changes

As projects evolve over time, changes to the underlying database schema are inevitable. Table structures may change, and fields get added, removed, renamed, or have their types modified. The ability to manage these changes while preserving data integrity is important for maintaining reliable applications. In this section, you will learn about version control for database schemas, migration tools like Flyway, techniques for data transformation during schema changes, and best practices for seamless updates with minimal system disruption.

随着项目随时间演进，对底层数据库 schema 的变更是不可避免的。表结构可能变化，字段可能被新增、移除、重命名或修改类型。在维护数据完整性的同时管理这些变更的能力，对于维持可靠的应用很重要。在本节中，你将学习数据库 schema 的版本控制、Flyway 之类的迁移工具、schema 变更期间的数据转换技术，以及以最小系统 disruption 实现无缝更新的最佳实践。

Using version control for data structures

Close your eyes and imagine your entire codebase stored without version control. That thought should send shivers down your spine. Just as you wouldn’t develop software without tracking changes or enabling streamlined collaboration, your database schema deserves the same protection.

闭上眼睛，想象你的整个代码库没有版本控制地存放着。那个念头应该让你脊背发凉。正如你不会在不跟踪变更、不启用顺畅协作的情况下开发软件，你的数据库 schema 也值得同样的保护。

Without version control, you risk losing critical history, overwriting colleagues’ work, and lacking the ability to roll back problematic changes. Your schema, the foundation of your data infrastructure, requires the same careful versioning that safeguards your application code.

没有版本控制，你就冒着丢失关键历史、覆盖同事工作、以及无法回滚有问题变更的风险。你的 schema 是数据基础设施的基础，需要与保护应用代码同样仔细的版本管理。

原书第 214 页

Tools like Flyway, Liquibase, and Rails Migrations provide frameworks for versioning database schemas. These tools track which schema changes have been applied to each environment, ensuring consistency across development, testing, and production.

Flyway、Liquibase 和 Rails Migrations 之类的工具为数据库 schema 版本化提供了框架。这些工具跟踪每个环境应用了哪些 schema 变更，确保开发、测试和生产环境之间的一致性。

Let’s look at a practical example with Flyway. Flyway takes a straightforward approach to database migrations. At its core, Flyway does the following:

我们看一个 Flyway 的实际例子。Flyway 对数据库迁移采取直截了当的方式。其核心工作如下：

  • Maintains a special table in your database (typically called flyway_schema_history) that tracks which migrations have been applied在你的数据库中维护一个特殊表（通常叫 flyway_schema_history），跟踪哪些迁移已被应用
  • Scans a designated folder for migration scripts that follow a specific naming convention扫描指定文件夹，查找遵循特定命名约定的迁移脚本
  • Compares the available scripts against what’s recorded in the history table把可用脚本与历史表中记录的内容对比
  • Executes any new scripts that haven’t been applied yet执行任何尚未应用的新脚本

For example, you might organize your migrations as SQL files with version numbers:

例如，你可以把迁移组织成带版本号的 SQL 文件：

V1__Create_users_table.sql
V2__Add_email_to_users.sql
V3__Create_orders_table.sql

Sequential Migrations
顺序迁移

Most migration tools, including Flyway, are designed to execute migrations sequentially. This means migrating from version 100 to version 250 requires running each migration script in order (100 → 101 → 102… → 250). While this might seem inefficient, it’s actually a safety feature that ensures data integrity and allows each migration to build properly on the previous state. Some advanced scenarios allow for “squashing” migrations or creating direct migration paths, but the sequential approach is the standard practice because it guarantees consistency and makes troubleshooting easier when issues arise.
大多数迁移工具（包括 Flyway）都设计为顺序执行迁移。这意味着从版本 100 迁移到 250 需要按顺序运行每个迁移脚本（100 → 101 → 102… → 250）。虽然这看起来低效，但它实际上是一个安全特性，确保数据完整性，并让每个迁移都能正确地基于前一个状态构建。一些高级场景允许“压缩”迁移或创建直接迁移路径，但顺序方式是标准做法，因为它保证一致性，并在问题出现时更容易排查。

The following are the most important practices for schema versioning:

以下是 schema 版本化最重要的实践：

  • Make each change script idempotent (can be run multiple times without harm)让每个变更脚本幂等（可以运行多次而无害）
  • Ensure that scripts are backward compatible whenever possible尽可能确保脚本向后兼容
  • Include both the change and any necessary data transformations in the same script把变更和任何必要的数据转换放在同一个脚本里

Managing data dependencies and transformations

When schema changes require data transformations, version them alongside your schema changes. This ensures that your database structure and its data remain in sync across all environments.

当 schema 变更需要数据转换时，把它们与 schema 变更一起版本化。这确保你的数据库结构和其数据在所有环境中保持同步。

原书第 215 页

Building on our Flyway example, migrations aren’t limited to SQL scripts. Flyway supports both SQL and Java-based migrations, giving you flexibility to handle complex transformations with the full power of your programming language:

在 Flyway 例子的基础上，迁移不限于 SQL 脚本。Flyway 同时支持 SQL 和基于 Java 的迁移，让你能灵活地用编程语言的全部能力处理复杂转换：

// V4__Add_Address_Components.java - Flyway Java-based migration
public class V4__Add_Address_Components implements JdbcMigration {

    public void migrate(Connection connection) throws Exception {
        // First, alter the schema to add new columns
        try (Statement stmt = connection.createStatement()) {
            stmt.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN street VARCHAR(255)");
            stmt.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN city VARCHAR(255)");
            stmt.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN state VARCHAR(255)");
            stmt.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN zip_code VARCHAR(10)");
            stmt.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN country VARCHAR(255)");
        }

        // Then, migrate the existing data
        try (PreparedStatement select =
        connection.prepareStatement("SELECT id, address FROM users");
             PreparedStatement update = connection.prepareStatement(
                "UPDATE users SET street = ?, city = ?, state = ?, zip_code = ?, " +
                "country = ? WHERE id = ?")) {

            ResultSet rs = select.executeQuery();
            while (rs.next()) {
                long id = rs.getLong("id");
                String fullAddress = rs.getString("address");

                // Parse components for new schema
                AddressComponents components = addressParser.parse(fullAddress);

                // Update user with new format
                update.setString(1, components.getStreet());
                update.setString(2, components.getCity());
                update.setString(3, components.getState());
                update.setString(4, components.getZipCode());
                update.setString(5, components.getCountry());
                update.setLong(6, id);
                update.executeUpdate();
            }
        }
    }
}

This code-based approach allows you to leverage your application’s existing business logic, handle complex parsing, and implement validation during migration that would be challenging with SQL alone.

这种基于代码的方式让你能利用应用已有的业务逻辑、处理复杂解析、并在迁移期间实现校验——这些单用 SQL 会很有挑战。

原书第 216 页

This approach ensures the following:

这种方式确保以下几点：

  • The schema change and data transformation are versioned together, maintaining consistency.schema 变更和数据转换一起版本化，保持一致性。
  • The migration is atomic—either both the schema and data changes succeed, or neither does.迁移是原子的——要么 schema 和数据变更都成功，要么都不成功。
  • You can track which environments have the transformation applied by using Flyway’s schema history.你可以用 Flyway 的 schema 历史跟踪哪些环境已应用了该转换。

For complex transformations, consider these options:

对于复杂转换，考虑以下选项：

  • Running transformations as background jobs to minimize system impact把转换作为后台作业运行，以最小化系统影响
  • Implementing a dual-write approach during transition periods在过渡期实现双写方式
  • Creating a rollback plan in case transformation issues arise创建回滚计划，以防转换出问题

Remember that data quality issues often surface during transformations. Be prepared to handle missing data, invalid formats, and edge cases you never anticipated. When working on data transformations, start with a small sample and validate the results thoroughly before processing your entire dataset. This approach can save you from considerable headaches.

记住，数据质量问题常常在转换期间浮出水面。做好准备处理缺失数据、无效格式和你从未预料到的边界情况。做数据转换时，从小样本开始，在处理整个数据集之前彻底验证结果。这种方式能帮你省去大量头疼事。

Wrapping Up

Data is the backbone of a large percentage of applications you will probably build throughout your career. While you might be tempted to focus solely on languages, frameworks, and tools, your ability to effectively work with data will be a valuable skill and will often determine your application’s success.

数据是你在职业生涯中可能构建的大部分应用的骨架。虽然你可能很想只专注于语言、框架和工具，但你高效处理数据的能力将是一项宝贵的技能，而且往往决定你应用的成败。

Throughout this chapter, we’ve explored various aspects of working with data:

在整章中，我们探索了处理数据的各个方面：

  • Understanding different data types and formats (structured versus unstructured)理解不同的数据类型和格式（结构化与非结构化）
  • Selecting appropriate database types for your specific use cases为具体用例选择合适的数据库类型
  • Implementing effective data persistence patterns and connection management实现有效的数据持久化模式和连接管理
  • Optimizing queries for better performance优化查询以获得更好性能
  • Planning for data growth and migrations为数据增长和迁移做规划

An important takeaway from this chapter is that there are rarely perfect solutions in data management, only appropriate ones for your specific application. No decision you make is finite, and you should try to make an informed decision about what data structures to use or what type of database to build on top of and move on. It’s better to make a decision based on your current requirements rather than playing the

本章一个重要的收获是：数据管理中很少有完美方案，只有适合你具体应用的方案。你做的任何决定都不是终局，你应该对使用什么数据结构、或在什么类型的数据库之上构建做出明智决策，然后继续前进。基于当前需求做决定，总比玩那种

原书第 217 页

what-if game for an application that might be around for the time period or user base you’re planning for.

“如果……会怎样”的游戏要好——你计划的那个时间段或用户规模，应用未必能活到那时候。

This is called overengineering, and it often leads to unnecessarily complex systems that are harder to maintain and adapt to actual needs. Instead, focus on solving today’s problems effectively while keeping your design reasonably flexible, rather than building elaborate architectures for hypothetical future scenarios.

这叫做过度设计，它常常导致不必要地复杂的系统，更难维护、更难适应实际需求。相反，专注于有效地解决今天的问题，同时让你的设计保持合理的灵活性，而不是为假设的未来场景构建精巧的架构。

Putting It into Practice

Working with data effectively is a skill that develops with experience. The concepts we’ve covered form the foundation of your data journey. But as with any craft, mastery comes through practical application.

高效处理数据是一项随经验增长的技能。我们讲的概念构成了你数据之旅的基础。但和任何手艺一样，精通来自实践。

Here are concrete ways you can start practicing these concepts today:

以下是你今天就可以开始实践这些概念的具体方式：

  • Analyze an existing application’s data model: Take an open source project on GitHub (like a simple ecommerce platform or blog engine) and map out its data structures. Identify the relationships among entities and evaluate whether the chosen database type suits the application’s needs.分析一个既有应用的数据模型：在 GitHub 上找一个开源项目（比如一个简单的电商平台或博客引擎），梳理它的数据结构。识别实体之间的关系，评估所选的数据库类型是否适合应用的需求。
  • Optimize a slow query: Find a query in your current project that’s underperforming. Use the EXPLAIN command to analyze its execution plan, then implement improvements like adding appropriate indexes or rewriting the query to be more efficient.优化一个慢查询：在你当前项目中找一个表现不佳的查询。用 EXPLAIN 命令分析它的执行计划，然后实施改进，比如加合适的索引或重写查询使其更高效。
  • Create a mini migration: Build a small application with a basic database schema, then practice evolving it. Add new fields, change data types, or split tables while preserving existing data. Use a migration tool like Flyway or Liquibase to manage these changes.做一个迷你迁移：构建一个带基本数据库 schema 的小应用，然后练习演进它。新增字段、改数据类型或拆表，同时保留现有数据。用 Flyway 或 Liquibase 之类的迁移工具管理这些变更。
  • Implement a basic caching strategy: Choose a read-heavy feature in an existing application and implement a simple caching layer. Measure performance before and after to quantify the improvement.实现一个基本缓存策略：在既有应用中选一个读多的功能，实现一个简单的缓存层。测量前后性能，量化改进。
  • Practice with multiple data formats: Take a dataset in one format (like CSV) and write code to transform it to another format (like JSON). Focus on handling edge cases like special characters, missing values, and proper type conversion.练习多种数据格式：拿一个格式（比如 CSV）的数据集，写代码把它转换成另一种格式（比如 JSON）。专注于处理特殊字符、缺失值和正确的类型转换等边界情况。
  • Design a storage strategy for unstructured data: Choose a scenario (like storing user-generated content) and design a solution that addresses both storage and efficient retrieval. Consider hybrid approaches that combine structured metadata with unstructured content.为非结构化数据设计存储策略：选一个场景（比如存储用户生成内容），设计一个同时解决存储和高效检索的方案。考虑把结构化元数据与非结构化内容结合的混合方式。
    • 原书第 218 页
  • Prototype a data intensive application: Build a small application that processes a large dataset—perhaps analyzing log files or visualizing public datasets. Focus on efficient data loading, transformation, and query optimization.原型做一个数据密集型应用：构建一个处理大型数据集的小应用——也许是分析日志文件或可视化公共数据集。专注于高效的数据加载、转换和查询优化。

Start small when implementing new data concepts. Jump in today with something simple that interests you! Each hands-on exercise builds your confidence and develops that special intuition for making smart data decisions. This practical knowledge will become one of your most valuable assets throughout your career, opening doors and helping you solve problems that might otherwise seem overwhelming. Remember, everyone starts somewhere: your first data project doesn’t need to be perfect; it just needs to exist!

实践新的数据概念时从小处开始。今天就从你感兴趣的简单东西入手！每个动手练习都在建立你的信心，培养做出明智数据决策的特殊直觉。这些实践知识将成为你整个职业生涯中最宝贵的资产之一，为你打开大门，帮你解决那些原本看起来难以应对的问题。记住，每个人都有起点：你的第一个数据项目不需要完美，它只需要存在！
